title: Ghost of Jupiter, NGC 3242
caption: The Ghost of Jupiter (NGC 3242) and its surrounding gas, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
celestial: Ghost of Jupiter, NGC 3242 · constellation Hydra

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Just above and to the right of the center of this wide view is the bright planetary nebula NGC 3242, nicknamed the Ghost of Jupiter. Around it spreads a much larger, fainter cloud of gas.

A planetary nebula forms when a dying star casts off its outer layers, and the exposed hot core makes that gas glow. Close-up images usually focus on the bright nebula itself, but this wide field captures what lies around it.

The nature of that extended cloud is still unknown. One possibility is that it is a shell of gas thrown off by NGC 3242 earlier, when the star was a red giant. Another is that it is simply a nearby cloud of interstellar gas being lit up by the planetary nebula.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Oxygen [O III] is shown in blue and hydrogen-alpha in orange.
filters: 499 nm · Optical Olll (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
656 nm · Optical Ha (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: The surrounding cloud is far too faint for the eye. Narrow filters and long exposures bring it out.

explore: Kitt Peak National Observatory's Mayall 4-meter telescope recorded the scene with its wide-field Mosaic camera on December 15th, 2006. North is to the left and east is down.
alt: A small bright nebula just above and right of center, surrounded by a large, faint cloud of gas.
